reference: Metadata contracts use Bash's documented type/help builtins and the pinned stock loadable's documented help text. FIFO operations are deferred; a future disposable VM must compare the loadable with GNU coreutils mkfifo and inspect FIFO type, permission bits, preserved preexisting paths, statuses, stdout, and stderr independently.
coverage: The candidate exposes mkfifo as a Bash builtin while candidate PATH is empty.
The short help synopsis matches the declared usage.
The full builtin help includes the FIFO description, default-mode and umask behavior, -m behavior, and symbolic-mode description.
Private FIFO fixtures check default permissions, octal and symbolic modes, multi-operand creation and partial failure, invalid modes, and argument errors.
exclusions: FIFOs are created only in the disposable fixture directory and are never connected to host IPC. Concurrent writer/reader behavior is outside this permission and creation suite.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash resolves mkfifo as a builtin with no executable search path. The expected token follows Bash type -t metadata semantics.
Check documented builtin help metadata without creating a FIFO. Bash help output must include the FIFO description and the documented default-mode, -m, and symbolic-mode details.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help mkfifo)
[[ $help_text == *"Create FIFOs (named pipes)."* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"using mode a=rw as modified by the current"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *umask* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"The -m option causes the file permission"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"octal number or a symbolic mode"* ]]
printf 'builtin help contract present\n'

cases.purpose: Require help -s to print the builtin's declared usage synopsis. The expected synopsis comes from mkfifo_struct.short_doc in the pinned Bash source and Bash help -s semantics.
cases.script:
usage_text=$(help -s mkfifo)
[[ $usage_text == *"mkfifo [-m mode] fifo_name [fifo_name ...]"* ]]
printf 'short usage synopsis present\n'

cases.purpose: Default FIFO permissions honor the creation mask.
An explicit mode overrides the creation mask.
Explicit symbolic permission classes override the creation mask.

cases.purpose: Create valid operands on either side of an existing file and preserve that file.
An invalid octal mode fails without creating a FIFO.
Missing operands return GNU failure status.
An explicit mode may include execute bits.
